title: Principality of Regensberg
capsule: The Principality of Regensburg (Fürstentum Regensburg) was a short-lived Napoleonic-era state created in 1803 when the mediatized prince-bishop Karl Theodor von Dalberg received secularized episcopal and abbatial territories around Regensburg as compensation under the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss. Dalberg served simultaneously as Napoleon's closest German ecclesiastical ally and from 1806 as Prince-Primate of the Confederation of the Rhine. In 1810 Napoleon transferred Regensburg to the Kingdom of Bavaria and compensated Dalberg with the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt, ending the principality's seven-year existence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's extent is clearly defined by 1803 secularization decrees and Bavarian annexation records; cartographic attestation for this Napoleonic period is good.
